 Share 14m ago 13.18 EST Half time: Newcastle 0-1 Arsenal
 Eze’s free-kick is punched away by Hornicek, the last action of a first half that ends with boos from the home fans. Arsenal are on course to go eight points clear at the top. They wore Newcastle down during an ultimately one-sided first half, with Kai Havertz and the scorer Eberechi Eze combining for a fine goal. This isn’t news, but Arsenal are a seriously good football team.
 Share 16m ago 13.15 EST 45 min: Fine block by Hall! Odegaard gets away on the left and slides an inviting low cross to Madueke, who looks certain to score until Hall gets round to deflect his shot over the bar. Brilliant defending.
 Share 17m ago 13.14 EST 43 min: Good save by Hornicek! Madueke robs Hall, who is having a dodgy spell, and sets off towards goal. He gallops into the area, just about keeps his balance and drives a low right-foot shot from the angle that is kicked away by Hornicek.
 Share 19m ago 13.12 EST 41 min Barnes has a speculative shot blocked after a decent raid down the left by Osula. That’s the first time in ages that Newcastle have penetrated the final third.
 Share 22m ago 13.10 EST 39 min Calafiori cuts inside from the right – don’t ask me, he’s the left-back – and screws a shot well wide.
 Gabriel may have an injury problem; he’s feeling his side. William Saliba is among the subs.
 Share 23m ago 13.09 EST 38 min “I’m sorry to hear that Charles Antaki’s lobster is too buttery and his diamond shoes are too tight (5.14pm),” writes Matt Dony. “The front three might not be Salah/Mane/Firmino (sob) but they’re doing a job. Whether Kari Tulinius likes it or not, I’d like to congratulate Arsenal on the successful defence of their title. Stick a fork in it. Roll on next season.”
 Share 23m ago 13.08 EST 37 min Newcastle will be frustrated that the goal stemmed from an error, and surprised that the man responsible was the usually excellent Lewis Hall. It was a split-second misjudgement that was punished ruthlessly by Havertz and Eze.
 Share 25m ago 13.07 EST 35 min “Such prescience,” says Richard Hirst. “What lottery numbers have you picked?”
 Pah, that’s an insult! The lottery is pure luck. But there’s nothing lucky about a stopped clock showing the correct time twice a day.
 Share 26m ago 13.05 EST Lewis Hall miscontrolled a long ball forward and was robbed by the ever-alert Havertz. He cut inside, 35 yards from goal, and angled a devastating through pass towards Eze, who swept an emphatic shot on the run past Hornicek. A fine goal: beautifully created, majestically taken.
 Share 28m ago 13.04 EST GOAL! Newcastle 0-1 Arsenal (Eze 33)
 A goal was coming, and when it did it was a beauty.
 View image in fullscreen Eberechi Eze beats Hornícek to give the Gunners the lead! Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters View image in fullscreen Photograph: David Price/AFC/Getty Images Share Updated at  13.09 EST 29m ago 13.02 EST 31 min Arsenal’s dominance has grown almost imperceptibly through this first half, and a goal is starting to feel imminent. Newcastle can’t get out.
 Share 32m ago 13.00 EST 27 min: Chance for Guimaraes! Madueke teases a couple of defenders on the edge of the area, then finds Rice on the outside. He clips an insouciant, inviting cross to the far post, where Bruno Guimaraes arrives late and studs the ball wide from eight yards. He was at full stretch so there wasn’t much more he could do.
 Share Updated at  13.01 EST 34m ago 12.57 EST 26 min Madueke wafts high over the bar from 15 yards. A very tough chance, especially as it was on his right foot.
 Share 37m ago 12.55 EST 24 min The Newcastle fans pay tribute to their former captain Bruno Guimares with a brief chorus of “one greedy gentleman”.
 Share 38m ago 12.54 EST 23 min Dedic is booked for pulling back Eze near the halfway line.
 Share 38m ago 12.53 EST 22 min Arsenal play through the Newcastle press, culminating in a shot from Havertz that whistles past the near post. Tough chance; Hornicek probably had the angle covered regardless.
 Share 43m ago 12.49 EST 18 min Dedic roars in celebration after conceding a throw-in with a slide tackle on Eze. Those celebrations aren’t to all tasted, but there’s no judgement here; you should see me punch the air when I think of a one-liner or stumble upon a statgasm.
 Share 45m ago 12.47 EST 16 min The pattern of the game is as expected: lots of possession for Arsenal , the occasional dangerous break from Newcastle. There’s your tactical analysis babes.
 Share 48m ago 12.43 EST 12 min Murphy cuts inside from the right, 25 yards from goal, and hits a speculative shot with his left foot. It takes a huge deflection off a Newcastle player, possibly Barnes, and bounces just wide with Raya beaten.
 Share Updated at  12.46 EST 51m ago 12.41 EST 10 min Hornicek farts around with the ball at his feet, then whips out a copy of War and Peace as Havertz closes in. Eventually Havertz makes a block tackle and the ball ricochets safely for Newcastle. Could’ve gone anywhere.
 Share 52m ago 12.40 EST 8 min Odegaard collects the ball in the centre circle, everything in front of him, and so nearly knifes a devastating through pass for the marauding Calafiori. In the end the ball ran through to Hornicek but it was a lovely try from Odegaard.
 Share 53m ago 12.38 EST 8 min “Hello Rob,” writes Kári Tulinius. “This Arsenal fan is feeling nervous about this match. Not because I think the Magpies are any good, they’re not, but because this season is starting to feel like a procession to the title already. It’s barely even winter yet. Only the Seagulls look high-flying enough to mount a challenge, and they usually don’t win a game in December. Things look so good that the wheels surely will come off. A match against an out-of-sorts Newcastle feels like the type of occasion where that might happen.”
 Relax, enjoy it. We’re alive!
 Share 54m ago 12.37 EST 6 min: Madueke hits the post
 Raya’s long ball is controlled beautifully on the edge of the D by Eze, who turns and finds Madueke on the right. He cuts inside Burn with ease and drives a low shot that hits the outside of the near post. Hornicek had it covered but even so, hitting the post is hitting the post.
 Share 1h ago 12.35 EST 5 min A hearty boo turns seamlessly into a disdainful cheer when a pass from Bruno Guimaraes goes astray. Crikey, can you imagine the silence if he roofs one from 25 yards like he did at Sunderland earlier in the season.
 View image in fullscreen Jacob Murphy gets away from Bruno Guimaraes. Photograph: Andy Buchanan/AFP/Getty Images Share Updated at  12.38 EST 1h ago 12.34 EST 4 min “Doubling up Rob!” says Mike Wiltsher. “Always a treat to see the goat’s name at the top of a MBM or OBO. Sorry to hear you haven’t been well but glad you are on the mend and great to have you back. Take care of yourself and thanks for all your sterling work.”
 Cheers Mike. I’m morally obliged to point out that Scott Murray is the goat of this particular format, but I appreciate it nonetheless.
 Share 1h ago 12.34 EST 3 min Jacob Murphy tries to drive a chip over David Raya from 50 yards. No, really. An audacious effort, well off target.
 Share 1h ago 12.31 EST 1 min Arsenal kick off to the sound of boos. I assume Bruno Guimaraes was somewhere near the ball.
 Share 1h ago 12.29 EST No Newcastle MBM is complete without the pre-match thoughts of Chris Paraskevas
 double quotation mark G’day Rob, hope you’re well! Last season’s meeting between these two sides at St James marked the end of one of the Premier League’s best managerial rivalries in recent years: Eddie Howe vs Mikel Arteta.
 It was the summit of the mountain Arsenal were yet to climb after Howe’s previous tactical victories over Arteta, which included his famous use of pressing centre-backs.
 Where Arteta’s Arsenal found that extra 10% last season, P.I.F and MJ’s Toon will need to do the same this time around. Arguably they’ll actually need to find an extra 100% because they’ve been so poor this season, but 10% is a great number because:
 a) 10% represents the likelihood of a win for NUFC tonight
 b) 10% represents my chances of ending the weekend in a fully functioning relationship like all my other friends (who aren’t really friends anymore because they never visit)
 c) 10% is the percentage of the world who believe ‘Sandpapergate’ is actually important
 c) 10% is how much of Grand Theft Auto VI I’ve finished so far...
 ....so there’s actually 90% of possibilities available (or 270% across multiple life disciplines, depending on your perspective).
 I really should have slept before this one, eh?
 That depends. What time is it in Australia? 7am on Monday?
 Share 1h ago 12.14 EST “There is an ebb and a flow to Arsenal’s front three, isn’t there?” writes Charles Antaki. “Eze, Havertz, Madueke – in any given game, one will delight and the other two disappoint; one will score and the other two will be all over the place; one will bring joy, and the other two will invite cursing and the gnashing of teeth. And all this is not to mention the chap lurking on the bench. Personally – I admit it – I’d rather have three fully functioning goal machines, but there we are.”
 We hate it when our teams become successful.
 Share 1h ago 12.07 EST Mikel Arteta on Bruno Guimaraes’s inclusion 
 double quotation mark He’s prepared emotionally; he knows to accept. We have to be very dominant emotionally to attack Newcastle in the way we want, and he’s ready to do that.

 Chelsea 1-4 Leeds, Tottenham 2-0 Ipswich, and more: football clockwatch – live Read more Share Updated at  12.45 EST 2h ago 11.29 EST Team news: Bruno Guimaraes starts
 Two changes for Newcastle from their draw with Fulham before the international break. Lewis Miley and Arsenal alumnus Joe Willock replaces Nico Gonzalez and Yoane Wissa.
 Arsenal, who beat Hull 1-0 a fortnight ago, bring in Eberechi Eze for Christos Tzolis. That means Bruno Guimaraes will start against his old club. A frighteningly strong bench includes the great William Saliba, who has yet to play this season because of a back injury.
 Newcastle (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Burn, Hall; Miley, Steur; Murphy, Willock, Barnes; Osula.
 Subs: Pope, Livramento, Botman, Schar, Nico Gonzalez, Wissa, Elanga, Fernandez-Pardo, Ramsey.
 Arsenal (4-3-3) Raya; Timber, Konsa, Gabriel, Calafiori; Odegaard, Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Havertz, Eze.
 Subs: Arrizabalaga, Saliba, Mosquera, White, Hincapie, Gyokeres, Tzolis, Merino, Lewis-Skelly.
 Referee Chris Kavanagh.

 Chelsea v Leeds, Tottenham v Ipswich, and more: football clockwatch – live Read more Share 2h ago 11.17 EST Manchester City’s draw with Fulham means Arsenal will go eight points clear if they win tonight. Second-placed Brighton play Hull tomorrow.
 Elliot Anderson halts Manchester City’s losing run but boos greet Fulham draw Read more Share Updated at  11.17 EST 2h ago 11.14 EST Ed Aarons Mikel Arteta has said Bukayo Saka may not return before Christmas as the Arsenal forward continues his rehabilitation from a thigh injury .
 Saka has been out since limping off against Bayern Munich at the end of last month, and it is understood he has yet to resume light training. Arteta revealed more tests during the international break confirmed the England forward did not need surgery and that he was expected to be out for another four weeks.
 When asked whether Saka could be fit for the game against Manchester United on 20 December, Arteta was unsure. “I cannot be that specific,” he said. “In four weeks’ time a lot of things can happen. Maybe it is three and then it is five.
 “At the end, there are a few elements. One is the healing of that tissue – and we cannot predict exactly when that tissue is going to be in the best condition to push it. Then there is the rehab plan that we have now, what he needs to do in the gym, what he needs to do in terms of treatment and on the field.”
 Bukayo Saka may not return for Arsenal before Christmas, Mikel Arteta admits Read more Share 2h ago 11.14 EST Louise Taylor With the temperature in Newcastle forecast to dip to 0C at kick-off , Matthias Jaissle is perhaps hoping that his team’s guests from north London (where a balmy 9C is predicted at 5.30pm) freeze in the Tyneside chill. Otherwise it is hard to envisage his young side overcoming a formidable looking Arsenal on a day when Newcastle’s head coach seeks what would be only his second win in seven games.
 Home fans will not merely be hurt by the sight of their much-missed former captain Bruno Guimarães wearing Arsenal colours but decidedly nervous about a fixture that precedes a run of tricky engagements involving a trip to Brighton and home dates with Manchester United and Sunderland.
 Jaissle’s cause could be helped should Mikel Arteta name Guimarães in his starting XI and the crowd respond to the once adored Brazilian’s defection by creating the sort of hostile atmosphere that might just galvanise a Newcastle team expected to contain the former Arsenal midfielder Joe Willock.
 Meanwhile Jaissle’s defence must be mindful of the threat posed by another Newcastle old boy in Mikel Merino.
 Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend Read more Share 3h ago 11.00 EST Preamble
 Arsenal have a unique relationship with the north of England. They’ve won titles at Anfield and Old Trafford, lost them at the Reebok Stadium, and there have been periods in history when every Arsenal trip beyond Watford Gap felt like a referendum on whether they had the necessary minerals.
 Mikel Arteta’s side aren’t much different. For years, St James’ Park was a symbol of their inability to take the final step to glory. That changed last September, when Gabriel’s 96th-minute winner set up a different neural pathway that ultimately led to Arsenal becoming champions for the first time since 2004.
 Newcastle (A) was a more intimidating prospect 14 months ago than it is today. St James’ Park hasn’t been much of a fortress this season, with Newcastle taking only five points from five home games under Matthias Jaissle. But just as Arsenal changed the narrative last season, so Newcastle can do the same today.
 Kick off 5.30pm.
